By Chris De Silva

Topic:AFL

Logan Morris (right) kicked all four of his goals in the first half as Brisbane recorded a 67-point win over Hawthorn at the Gabba. (Getty Images: Chris Hyde)

It's taken a long time to be on display but Chris Fagan is a happy man about the prospect of having a trio of tall forwards at his disposal heading into the AFL finals.

For the first time Oscar Allen joined Eric Hipwood and Logan Morris in a Brisbane Lions forward line on Friday night as the premiers outclassed Hawthorn by 67 points at a packed Gabba.

Morris kicked four first-half goals while Hipwood chipped in with two of his own to leave Fagan confident he has a new weapon in his armory as the Lions chase a premiership three-peat.

"I liked it," Fagan said.

"Oscar didn't have a lot of the ball, but that's often what happens when you have three of them there.

"But between them, they caused a bit of chaos. The ball hit the deck and the lads up there did a pretty good job of cleaning up when it did."

The biggest beneficiary of that chaos was Kai Lohmann, who kicked five goals in a best-on-ground performance that had Fagan beaming for his small forward.

"He's just got his pressure right," Fagan said.

"He doesn't have to worry about doing all those freakish things. They just happen."When he focuses entirely on putting pressure on, his game seems to come together."

Hawthorn coach Sam Mitchell knows his team failed to deliver, but it doesn't have him reaching for the panic button.

With just two rounds to go before finals, the 11-goal defeat opens the door on the third-placed Hawks potentially missing a top four spot as the chasing pack breathe down their necks.

The Lions are now two points behind the Hawks on the ladder while Adelaide and Melbourne sit just a further four points back with their games yet to come this weekend.

It means the Hawks — who haven't beaten a top 10 team since May — need to win next weekend's clash with Collingwood at the MCG to ensure they'll retain that hard-earned third position, especially with the Lions set to host out-of-form Gold Coast in a Queensland derby at the Gabba.

Mitchell made no bones that Friday's display wasn't good enough and his team were well beaten, with the challenge now being to show the AFL world that performance was a one-off.

"We're better than that and we're going to have to prove it," Mitchell said.

"We've got to learn some lessons from that game.

"By the end of this round we'll be sitting third on the ladder, coming into two games to go, playing Collingwood on a Saturday night.

"So by the time we lick our wounds and spend a couple of days being annoyed at looking backwards, pretty quickly we'll recognise that we're a good side and ready to move forwards."

By Chris De Silva

Hawthorn coach Sam Mitchell doesn't seem too fazed by that result.

Mitchell spoke a lot, but the general gist of his press conference was summed up by these words:

"We were outclassed tonight, I think we're better than that. We saw it as an opportunity to compete against the best and we weren't up to it.

"We're a better side than tonight [showed], and we'll have to prove that next week."

By Chris De Silva

Brisbane has bounced back from last week's thumping by Carlton to thrash Hawthorn by 67 points at the Gabba.

Led by Kai Lohmann's five-goal haul, the premiers stayed firmly in the top four hunt with a convincing 18.17 (125) to 8.10 (58) win over the third-placed Hawks.

The victory was a perfect response to the 76-point loss to the Blues as the Lions celebrated a double milestone night with Jarrod Berry making his 200th AFL appearance and veteran defender Ryan Lester marking his 250th AFL game with a late goal that delighted the sell-out crowd.

Defeat for Sam Mitchell's team ends a four-game winning run ahead of next weekend's clash with Collingwood at the MCG and will raise questions heading into the finals about their genuine premiership credentials.

In a week where his own visit to Magpies HQ was a focus, Lachie Neale was a standout for the Lions with 35 disposals, seven marks, eight tackles and six clearances.

As well as Lohmann, the Lions had four multiple goalkickers with Logan Morris kicking four majors in the first half, Charlie Cameron booting three and Eric Hipwood scored two including a booming third-quarter shot from well outside 50.

Will Ashcroft had a game-high 39 disposals including 13 score involvements while Harris Andrews delivered another defensive masterclass, snaffling 10 marks as the Hawks forward line struggled to get clean ball all night.

The Hawks though were also guilty of missing crucial chances in the opening two quarters with Harry Morrison and Sam Butler both offending as the Lions surged into a winning position.

The hosts were only six clear at the end of the first term but scored three quickfire goals at the start of the second to break the game open and never looked back, the Hawks unable to mount any meaningful resistance.

In the end Jack Gunston finished with three majors while Josh Ward had 28 disposals but it was a disappointing night for the Hawks who were simply second-best across the park.

Here's a look at how the final numbers panned out from tonight:

Key Event

By Chris De Silva

A couple of Hawthorn players spoil themselves in a marking contest right on the siren, and that is symbolic of the type of night the Hawks have had.

They've been outclassed from the first siren to the last and the Lions have shown why you cannot count them out of this year's premiership hunt.

After such a disappointing weekend last week, they send out an ominous warning to the rest of the competition by dismantling a top-four side.

Will Ashcroft finishes with a game-high 39 disposals and also collected 13 score involvements, seven clearances and six intercepts.

The forward combo of Kai Lohmann (5.2) and Logan Morris (4.1) was absolutely lethal, and made Hawthorn's defence look decidedly old tonight.

A word as well to the ageless Lachie Neale, who finishes with 35 touches, 10 score involvements, eight tackles, six clearances and six intercepts.

By Chris De Silva

Charlie Cameron drills his third goal of the night and makes sure he counts them on his fingers after taking a nice one-handed mark inside 50.

The Lions are now up by 73 points. This is a proper, proper belting.

By Chris De Silva

Jarman Impey is protesting for God knows why after almost decapitating Cam Rayner with some front-on contact in a marking contest.

It was a wonderful chipped kick inside 50 from Lachie Neale, who has quietly ticked along to 33 touches, that found Rayner.

Rayner goes back and drills the set shot from directly in front to extend the margin to 67 points.

By Chris De Silva

How good is this!

Sam Draper takes a mark deep inside 50 and he unselfishly hands it off for Ryan Lester, who has snuck forward to kick a rare goal in his 250th career match.

He's absolutely mobbed by his teammates after that too!

Lester has been with the Lions since 2011, through the absolute grimmest times, and now he is reaping the rewards at the back end of his career.

He is one of the great culture-setters in the competition.

By Chris De Silva

Some real 2017 Russell Westbrook-level stat padding going on from Will Ashcroft right now.

He's up to 35 touches for the match now, 11 of them have come in this final quarter.

By Chris De Silva

Kai Lohmann is putting on an absolute small forward masterclass tonight!

He takes a mark in the pocket and decides to go for a left-footed snap from the boundary this time, and absolutely flushes it.

Lohmann's got 23 touches and 5.2 for the night. This is some vintage Jason Akermanis stuff.

By Chris De Silva

It feels like the Hawks might be down huge if not for a few free kicks inside 50 today.

Josh Weddle gets one this time after being infringed upon in a marking contest and he drills the set shot via a snap.

The result is academic at this point, but percentage might be a factor when it comes to this top four race.

By Chris De Silva

What a finish this is from Kai Lohmann!

Cam Rayner sends the ball inside 50 and Lohmann crumbs the ball beautifully and snaps on the left boot as he falls to the ground.

The finish is so good that Jarman Impey can't do anything but help Lohmann to his feet after the goal.

Brisbane by 55 points now. They might have their eyes on wiping out all of last week's big percentage deficit.

By Chris De Silva

It feels a little like the Lions have snatched the Hawks souls tonight.

The Lions keep hammering the ball inside 50 here, and luckily for the Hawks, it's not yielded a goal yet.

Cam Rayner the latest Lion to miss, this one coming from a very gettable set shot, leaving Brisbane 0.3 for the quarter.

They've already racked up four forward half intercepts for the quarter.

Key Event

By Chris De Silva

It's been some big brother, little brother stuff out here through three quarters tonight.

The Hawks came into this running hot and looking to get one over the champs, and the champs have reminded the Hawks and the rest of the comp who they are.

It's been clinical and ruthless from Brisbane all over the ground, and Hawthorn has looked second rate, to be brutally honest.

Hawthorn's Josh Ward is the leading ball-winner with 25 touches and he's also got five clearances, while Will Ashcroft leads the way for the Lions with 24 touches and five clearances of his own.

Kai Lohmann has also put together an incredibly damaging game up forward. He's kicked 3.2 and has 18 touches and has been a right nuisance all night.

Hawthorn's 42 inside 50s have yielded just 44 points tonight, and that's probably why they're hellbent on getting Ben King to the club next year.

One more quarter to go, Brisbane by 46 points, surely this one is done.

By Chris De Silva

Dan Annable with a brilliant finish on the left foot and he's mobbed by his teammates after his first goal at the AFL level!

Another shocking moment for Tom Barrass, who drops a regulation mark, and some brilliant forward pressure from Logan Morris as he tackles Josh Weddle forces the ball loose.

Annable picks it up and snaps brilliantly.

That is a big goal on the stroke of three-quarter-time.

By Chris De Silva

Dylan Moore drills a set shot to keep the Hawks in touch with a minute left in the quarter.

The Hawks are able to transition after a really questionable deliberate/lasso call against the Lions at half forward.

By Chris De Silva

I'll tell you what, Josh Battle and Tom Barrass are having absolute STINKERS out there tonight.

This time it's Battle with a fumble on a groundball, and the Lions are able to force the turnover in the middle of the ground again.

Lachie Neale sends the ball inside 50 where Kai Lohmann completely outpoints Karl Amon in a marking contest before kicking his third goal via the set shot.
